get.description: Same filters and access rule as the inbox. At most 50,000 rows (more → 422, narrow the filters). Every export is in the audit log with its filters and row count (a search is recorded only by its length), and on each exported lead's timeline. The file contains personal data. Although it is a GET, it needs the X-CSRF-Token header (403 without it), and a Sec-Fetch-Site header other than same-origin is refused (403): download it with fetch and save the blob, never with a plain link. Columns: reference, created_at, name, phone, email, project, configuration, source, status, lost_reason, lost_reason_note, owner, assigned_at, read_at, last_activity_at, message, page_url, referrer, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content, gclid, gbraid, wbraid, fbclid, msclkid, preferred_bhk, budget_max_inr, preferred_contact_time, language, consent_text_version, consented_at, consent_note, marketing_consent, duplicate_of, is_spam, is_sample, erased_at.

delete.description: Erases this lead and its whole duplicate group (the lead it repeats and every lead that repeats it); `scope=person` also erases every other lead with the same phone number (`same_phone_count` on the lead says how many). Name and phone become '[erased]'; email, message, page URL, referrer, click ids, preferred contact time and the UTM term and content are removed; note texts, the lost-reason note and visit notes are replaced or removed, in the timeline and stored events too. The reference, stage, reason code, source, UTM source/medium/campaign, project, timestamps and the consent record's version and time stay. Audited with the scope and count; can't be undone. Leads already erased are skipped (204 again).
